fields.statement: At d8d01e896 on linux/amd64 I ran the branch's install.sh hands-on against the real GitHub releases. cat install.sh | HOME=<scratch> sh fetched the release manifest and installed rhiza v0.1.0 into <scratch>/.local/bin (rhiza version: v0.1.0) and printed the PATH hint. cat install.sh | sh -s -- --channel latest --dir <scratch> installed v0.1.1-main.14+38cee74, which ran. For tamper, I served the real release manifest from a local mirror via RHIZA_INSTALL_BASE_URL with the linux/amd64 archive's bytes altered: it exited 1 with 'sha256 mismatch ... nothing installed', and the --dir stayed empty. sh -s -- --help printed the help under a pipe; --channel nope exited 1. go test -trimpath -count=1 ./tools/install -run TestInstallScript passed.

At d8d01e896 I followed the README install section by hand. Its install.sh one-liner and the --channel latest form both installed working binaries (v0.1.0 and v0.1.1-main.14+38cee74). Both manifest URLs it names resolve and are the ones the script fetches. sha256sum of the real rhiza_0.1.0_linux_amd64.tar.gz matched its manifest entry. gh attestation verify <archive> --repo dphaener/rhiza exited 0, with source repo dphaener/rhiza and signer release.yml@refs/tags/v0.1.0. It exited 1 for an altered copy. go install remains documented.
